stem: Which class contains the problems whose proposed solutions can be checked in polynomial time?
explanation: NP is the class of problems whose solutions can be verified in polynomial time.

stem: Who introduced the concept of NP-completeness in 1971?
Which problem was the first shown to be NP-complete, by the Cook–Levin theorem?
explanation: The Cook–Levin theorem shows SAT is NP-complete: every NP problem reduces to it.

stem: Which conditions together make a decision problem L NP-complete?

options.text: Every problem in NP reduces to L in polynomial time
L can be solved in polynomial time

explanation: NP-complete means in NP and NP-hard; no polynomial algorithm is known, and NP problems are decidable.

stem: A problem that satisfies only 'every NP problem reduces to it in polynomial time' is called NP-hard.
explanation: NP-hard needs only the reduction property; NP-complete also requires membership in NP.

stem: Which are listed as open problems in computational complexity?
explanation: P versus NP, circuit lower bounds and de-randomization are open; propositional logic is known to be decidable.

stem: Which reduction is presented in the course?

options.text: 3SAT reduces in polynomial time to CLIQUE

explanation: Theorem 8.3 reduces 3SAT to CLIQUE: each clause becomes a triple of nodes.

stem: Which one is not a complexity class?
explanation: PCP is the Post Correspondence Problem; P, NP and PSPACE are complexity classes.
source: CSC 552 Study Session 5; CSC 552 Study Session 7
